nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function BPNT2/IMPAD1 alleles abolish or severely reduce the catalytic activity of gPAPP, the Golgi-lumenal 3'-phosphatase whose known substrate is the sulfotransferase by-product 3'-phosphoadenosine 5'-phosphate (PAP). Loss of this activity removes the only characterised route for clearing PAP from the Golgi lumen.

nodes.description: Reduced growth-plate signalling and proliferation acting on a defective cartilage template disorganise endochondral bone formation, producing the chondrodysplasia: shortening of the long bones and marked shortening of the tubular bones of the hands.

The large joints do not form or do not remain reduced, which is the basis of the congenital dislocations that name the disorder. The node is deliberately named for the outcome rather than for a mechanism, because two different mechanisms are on the table and neither is established in BPNT2-deficient tissue. One is mechanical: joint capsule, ligament and articular surfaces built from undersulfated proteoglycan lack the competence to hold a joint reduced. The other is developmental: the Impad1-null mouse is reported to misposition and misorient its interphalangeal joints, which would make this a patterning failure rather than a failure of tissue strength. The developmental account fits the congenital onset better, and the two are distinguishable by whether joints form in the wrong place or form correctly and then fail.

nodes.description: Accumulated PAP is understood to inhibit the Golgi glycosaminoglycan sulfotransferases, so sulfate transfer onto growing chondroitin and heparan sulfate chains falls even though the transferases themselves are intact and the donor PAPS is made normally. This distinguishes gPAPP deficiency from CHST3 disease (a single transferase is absent), from SLC26A2 disease (sulfate uptake fails) and from PAPSS2 disease (donor synthesis fails).

nodes.description: Chondroitin sulfate chains are assembled but undersulfated. In the Impad1-null mouse the change is a fall in 4-O-sulfated chondroitin sulfate with a reciprocal rise in the non-sulfated species, together with a smaller shift of the same kind in heparan sulfate; the heparan sulfate shift was measured in lung. Chain synthesis itself is not blocked, which separates this disorder from the linkeropathies and the chain-elongation defects.
